title: The Lauriston Gardens Mystery
question: Today, can Watson see what Sherlock Holmes sees?

sitting_room.described: The hearth end of the first-floor sitting-room of 221B Baker Street, 1881: two broad sash windows in the FAR wall over Baker Street, a black iron grate under a white marble mantelpiece in the LEFT wall, the panelled door to the landing in the RIGHT wall, a red patterned Turkey carpet, buff striped wallpaper, two worn armchairs at the hearth, bookshelves flanking the chimney breast, mid-morning: a coal fire burning in the grate, a breakfast table pushed back under the windows, and a sheet of blue-grey notepaper lying open on the arm of the basket chair.
sitting_room.landmark: the white marble mantelpiece over the black iron grate
sitting_room.route: from the basket chair at the room's centre to the tiled kerb at the chimney breast
sitting_room.geometry: The camera keeps to the carpet's centre on the near side of the room, so the two broad windows stand in the FAR wall, the marble mantelpiece and its grate hold the LEFT edge from the top of frame to the tiled kerb at the bottom, and the panelled landing door stands at the RIGHT. The worn basket chair sits in the RIGHT half of frame turned square to the grate.

cab.described: The inside of a black two-wheeled hansom cab on the Brixton Road, 1881, in a dun-coloured morning fog: two men side by side on one buttoned leather seat under the folding hood, the black folding doors closed across their knees, a brass side-lamp burning at the front corner, and the fog-grey street sliding past beyond the doors.
cab.landmark: the brass side-lamp burning at the front corner of the cab
cab.route: from the near end of the buttoned seat across to the far end under the hood
cab.geometry: The camera rides on the cab's own near side facing the two men, so the buttoned leather seat runs across the bottom of frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, the folding hood closes the TOP of frame behind their heads, the closed black doors cross the frame at their knees, and the fog-grey street shows beyond the doors at the LEFT edge. Watson keeps the LEFT half of frame and Holmes the RIGHT for every panel.

garden_path.described: The front garden of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens, off the Brixton Road, a foggy March morning: a shabby brick terrace house standing back from the street behind a small garden of sickly plants, three tiers of blank curtainless windows with a yellowed TO LET card in one pane, a narrow path of yellow clay and gravel crossing the garden to the front door, a three-foot brick wall with wooden rails along its top at the street, and a dun-coloured fog lying over the house-tops, seen from the street side: the yellow clay path crossing to the door, the low brick wall and its wooden rails along the near edge, and the sickly plants standing in wet soil either side of the path.
garden_path.landmark: the front door of Number 3 at the head of the clay path
garden_path.route: from the wooden rails at the street wall, along the yellow clay path, to the front door
garden_path.geometry: The path runs from the BOTTOM of frame toward the TOP. The three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails cross the BOTTOM of frame nearest the camera; the yellow clay path runs up the CENTRE with wet soil and sickly plants either side; the house front rises across the whole TOP of frame with its three tiers of blank windows, and the front door stands at the head of the path, growing from a hand's width to the full height of the frame along the route. The camera keeps to the path's LEFT side for every panel.
garden_path.crowd: one stalwart police constable in a tall helmet leaning against the brick wall, and five or six loafers in caps craning over the rails behind him

hall.described: The bare front hall of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens, off the Brixton Road, a foggy March morning: a shabby brick terrace house standing back from the street behind a small garden of sickly plants, three tiers of blank curtainless windows with a yellowed TO LET card in one pane, a narrow path of yellow clay and gravel crossing the garden to the front door, a three-foot brick wall with wooden rails along its top at the street, and a dun-coloured fog lying over the house-tops: stripped floorboards, a papered wall with the paper hanging loose in strips, an open front door letting the fog-grey daylight in from the LEFT, and the doorway to the front room standing open at the RIGHT.
hall.landmark: the open doorway to the front room
hall.route: from the open front door to the doorway of the front room at the hall's far end
hall.geometry: The open front door and its fog-grey daylight hold the LEFT edge of frame from the top to the floorboards at the bottom; the stripped hall floor runs up the CENTRE away from the camera; the loose-papered wall holds the RIGHT edge; and the open doorway to the front room stands at the TOP RIGHT, growing along the route. The camera keeps to the hall's LEFT wall for every panel.

front_room.described: The front room of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens, off the Brixton Road, a foggy March morning: a shabby brick terrace house standing back from the street behind a small garden of sickly plants, three tiers of blank curtainless windows with a yellowed TO LET card in one pane, a narrow path of yellow clay and gravel crossing the garden to the front door, a three-foot brick wall with wooden rails along its top at the street, and a dun-coloured fog lying over the house-tops, bare of furniture: a wide dusty floor of stripped boards, a thick coat of dust on every surface, wallpaper hanging away from the plaster in strips, one tall curtainless window in the FAR wall giving flat fog-grey daylight, a white marble mantelpiece with a stump of red wax candle on it, and a well-dressed man lying on his back in the middle of the floor.
front_room.landmark: the tall curtainless window in the far wall
front_room.route: from the doorway at the room's near side to the tall window in the far wall
front_room.geometry: The tall curtainless window stands in the CENTRE of the FAR wall and gives all the light; the white marble mantelpiece holds the LEFT edge with the candle stump on it; the dusty floorboards run from the BOTTOM of frame away to the far wall; the dead man lies across the CENTRE of the floor with his feet toward the window. The camera keeps to the doorway side of the body for every panel.

corner_wall.described: The darkest corner of the front room of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens, off the Brixton Road, a foggy March morning: a shabby brick terrace house standing back from the street behind a small garden of sickly plants, three tiers of blank curtainless windows with a yellowed TO LET card in one pane, a narrow path of yellow clay and gravel crossing the garden to the front door, a three-foot brick wall with wooden rails along its top at the street, and a dun-coloured fog lying over the house-tops, where the hanging wallpaper has peeled away to leave a yellow square of coarse bare plaster, the stripped floorboards meeting the skirting below it, and the flat fog-grey daylight from the far window reaching this corner faintly.
corner_wall.landmark: the yellow square of bare plaster where the paper has peeled away
corner_wall.route: from the middle of the room to the peeled corner at the far wall
corner_wall.geometry: The yellow square of bare plaster fills the upper CENTRE of frame with the hanging paper curling away either side of it; the two walls meet in a vertical line at the RIGHT of CENTRE; the skirting and the dusty floorboards cross the BOTTOM of frame. The camera faces into the corner for every panel and keeps the room's window behind it at the LEFT.

shots.frame: Close on Holmes in the basket chair at the fire, bare-headed, pale, dark hair swept back, the bottle-green velvet lapel and open white collar, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the white marble mantelpiece holding the LEFT edge.
shots.motion: Holmes turns his head from the fire toward the camera and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on his face; his eyebrows lift a little; his thin hand comes up open at his collarbone.
shots.camera: on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, level with the seated man's eyes and a long stride from the basket chair, a 100mm lens turned on his face. The white marble mantelpiece holds the LEFT edge and the amber grate throws its light from there
shots.at_rest: Holmes sits well back in the worn leather basket chair at the hearth with both boots on the red Turkey carpet, bare-headed, his dark hair swept back from the high forehead. The bottle-green velvet lapel lies open at his chest over the white shirt collar, and his thin hands rest one on each arm of the chair. Low red coals burn in the black iron grate at the LEFT, the buff striped wallpaper and the bookshelves stand behind him, and the two broad windows are small and grey beyond his shoulder
shots.turn: a parlour trick -> a man who reads hands
shots.why: Opens on the answer to episode 2's last line, so the two chapters lock together, and shows Holmes explaining rather than performing.

cuts.frame: Insert on the blue-grey notepaper lying open on the wicker chair arm, close-written in black ink, the fire's amber light across it.
cuts.motion: The near edge of the sheet lifts a finger's width as a thin hand takes it, and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth.
cuts.camera: on the carpet at the near side of the hearth, at the height of the chair's woven arm and angled down onto it, a forearm's length from the paper, a 50mm lens turned on the written sheet. The amber firelight crosses the wicker from the LEFT
cuts.at_rest: The blue-grey notepaper lies open and flat on the woven wicker arm of the basket chair, close-written in black ink from edge to edge, a signature standing alone at its foot, the woven arm running across the frame, the red Turkey carpet lying beyond it, the amber light of the grate crossing the paper from the LEFT, the bare wicker running out either side of the sheet, and the room behind the chair falling away out of focus

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes turned to Watson across the hearth, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the coal fire amber at the LEFT edge and the grey windows small beyond his shoulder, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes lifts one hand and turns its back toward the camera as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his fingers spread and close again; his eyes come round to the fire.
shots.camera: on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, level with Holmes's eyes and two yards from him, a 85mm lens turned across the hearth. The coal grate lies at the LEFT edge and the two broad windows stand small and grey beyond his shoulder
shots.at_rest: Holmes is turned from the fire toward Watson across the hearth, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet jacket open over the white shirt collar, his head in the RIGHT half of frame. His lips are together with the line on them and his hands are down at the chair. The coal fire burns amber in the black grate at the LEFT edge, the white marble mantelpiece stands above it, and the red Turkey carpet runs out of frame at the BOTTOM
shots.turn: an unexplained trick -> a method anyone could follow
shots.why: The chapter's own answer to the button of episode 2, spoken on camera; it is the method the rest of the episode tests.

shots.frame: Insert square on the blue-grey note held open in two bare sunburnt hands, the black ink close-written across it from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge of frame, a signature standing alone at the foot.
shots.motion: The sheet turns a few degrees flat toward the camera as the hands bring it up, and the camera pushes straight in on the written page.
shots.camera: on the carpet at the hearth, level with the held sheet and a forearm's length from it, square on to the paper, a 50mm lens turned on the written page. The firelight comes from the LEFT and the room behind falls away out of focus
shots.at_rest: The blue-grey note is held open in two bare sunburnt hands, the thumbs flat on its near face and the fingers behind it, the black ink close-written across the sheet from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge with a signature standing alone at the foot. Watson's white shirt cuffs show at both wrists below the brown tweed sleeves. The hearth's amber light lies along the paper from the LEFT and the sitting-room beyond the sheet is soft and dark
shots.turn: a quiet morning -> a body in an empty house
shots.why: The case arrives as an object, so the audience reads it before either man speaks about it.

cuts.frame: Close on Watson standing at the hearth with the blue-grey note open in both bare sunburnt hands, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the firelight along one cheek.
cuts.motion: Watson's eyes travel down the sheet to its foot and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on his face.
cuts.camera: on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, level with Watson's eyes and a long stride from him, a 100mm lens turned on his face. The amber grate throws its light across one cheek from the LEFT
cuts.at_rest: Watson stands at the hearth with both boots on the red Turkey carpet, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, the brown tweed overcoat open at the front, the tweed waistcoat beneath it, its gold watch chain across the waistcoat, the blue-grey note open in both bare sunburnt hands below his chin, the firelight along his near cheek from the LEFT, the white marble mantelpiece behind his shoulder, the bookshelves dark beyond it, and the black walking stick leaning on the chair at the RIGHT with its silver ball knob uppermost

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes risen from the basket chair with his overcoat half onto one shoulder, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the mantelpiece at the LEFT edge and the grey windows behind him, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes swings the overcoat up onto his far shoulder as he speaks the line and the camera pulls back a hand's breadth; his arm goes into the second sleeve; his eyes come round to the door.
shots.camera: on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, level with Holmes's shoulder and two yards from him, a 85mm lens turned on him as he rises. The mantelpiece holds the LEFT edge and the grey windows stand behind him
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands clear of the basket chair with his overcoat half onto one shoulder, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet jacket showing at the open front. His head is a quarter of the frame's height and his lips are together with the line on them. The white marble mantelpiece and its grate stand at the LEFT edge, the two broad windows give flat grey daylight behind him, and the empty basket chair is beside his knee
shots.turn: no crime to detect -> a crime worth the coat
shots.why: Holmes changing state from apathy to energy is the chapter's engine, and it is a whole-body action a camera can photograph.

shots.frame: Medium inside the hansom from its near side: the two men side by side on the buttoned leather seat, Watson in the LEFT half and Holmes in the RIGHT, the folding hood closing the TOP of frame, the closed black doors across their knees and the fog-grey street beyond at the LEFT edge.
shots.motion: The two men sway together a hand's breadth as the cab takes the road, and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth over the closed doors.
shots.camera: on the near side of the hansom looking in across the closed black doors, level with the seated men's chests and an arm's length from their knees, a 35mm lens turned on the pair. The folding hood closes the TOP of frame
shots.at_rest: Watson and Holmes sit side by side on the one buttoned leather seat under the folding hood, Watson in the LEFT half in his brown tweed overcoat with the waistcoat and watch chain beneath it, his right hand on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick, Holmes in the RIGHT half in the bottle-green velvet with his hands loose on his knees. The black folding doors are closed across both their knees, the brass side-lamp burns at the front corner, and the fog-grey street stands beyond the doors at the LEFT edge
shots.turn: a room -> the city between them and it
shots.why: The journey is the only air the episode gets between two interiors, and the fog is the chapter's own weather.

cuts.frame: Insert on the brass side-lamp burning at the cab's front corner, the fog-grey street sliding past beyond it, beads of wet standing on the black paint.
cuts.motion: One bead of wet runs a thumb's length down the black paint and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on the lamp.
cuts.camera: outside the cab at the front corner, level with the lamp and a forearm's length from it, a 50mm lens turned on the burning brass. The fog-grey street slides past beyond it
cuts.at_rest: The brass side-lamp burns steadily at the cab's front corner, its flame upright behind the glass, the polished brass wet and beaded with standing drops. The black painted bodywork runs away below it, beads of wet standing along the paint. Beyond the lamp the dun-coloured fog lies over the Brixton Road and the wet cobbles carry the smeared amber of other lamps

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes on the seat's far side under the hood, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the fog-grey street beyond the closed doors at the LEFT edge, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes turns his face from the passing street toward Watson as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his bare hand lifts from his knee and settles again; his eyes go back to the street.
shots.camera: on the seat's near side under the hood, level with Holmes's eyes and an arm's length from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The closed doors and the fog-grey street lie at the LEFT edge
shots.at_rest: Holmes sits on the seat's far side under the folding hood, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet collar turned up at his throat above the white shirt, his head in the RIGHT half of frame. His lips are together with the line on them and one bare hand rests on his knee. The buttoned leather of the seat stands behind his shoulder, the black folding doors are closed across his knees, and the fog-grey street slides past beyond them at the LEFT edge
shots.turn: urgency -> a man discussing violins
shots.why: Holmes's calm is the thing Watson cannot forgive, and it is the chapter's best character beat before the body.

shots.frame: Close on Watson on the seat's near side, bare-headed, sunburnt, thin waxed moustache, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the buttoned leather behind his shoulder and the fog-grey street at the LEFT edge.
shots.motion: Watson's eyes leave Holmes and travel out to the passing street, and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on his face.
shots.camera: on the seat's far side under the hood, level with Watson's eyes and an arm's length from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The fog-grey street lies beyond the doors at the LEFT edge
shots.at_rest: Watson sits on the seat's near side, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, the brown tweed overcoat open over the tweed waistcoat and its watch chain, his right hand closed on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick between his knees. The buttoned leather stands behind his shoulder, the brass side-lamp burns at the front corner at the LEFT, and the fog-grey street slides past beyond the closed black doors
shots.turn: impatience -> a silence he keeps
shots.why: Watson's own state, and the first sign that this chapter will be about what he can and cannot see.

cuts.frame: Insert past the closed black doors: the fog-grey Brixton Road sliding by, a lamp post and a shuttered shop front standing out of the dun-coloured fog and going again.
cuts.motion: The lamp post travels from the CENTRE of frame out past the LEFT edge and the camera holds on the fog beyond it.
cuts.camera: on the seat looking out past the closed black doors, level with the doors' top rail, a 50mm lens turned on the passing street. The fog stands grey beyond the paintwork
cuts.at_rest: The black folding doors are closed across the frame's BOTTOM and the dun-coloured fog lies over the Brixton Road beyond them. A cast-iron lamp post stands out of the fog at the CENTRE with its flame small and amber, a shuttered shop front behind it, the wet cobbles carrying the smeared light. The black paintwork of the doors stands steady across the BOTTOM and the fog closes over everything beyond twenty feet

shots.frame: Wide from the street side: the brick front of Number 3 rising across the whole TOP of frame with three tiers of blank curtainless windows, the yellow clay path running up the CENTRE to the front door, the three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails crossing the BOTTOM of frame.
shots.motion: The fog drifts a hand's breadth across the house front and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth up the path toward the door.
shots.camera: on the street pavement outside the wooden rails, at a standing man's eye height, square on to the house front, a 35mm lens turned up the clay path. The three-foot brick wall and its rails cross the BOTTOM of frame
shots.at_rest: The shabby brick front of Number 3 rises across the whole TOP of frame with three tiers of blank curtainless windows, the front door shut at the head of the path. The narrow path of yellow clay and gravel runs up the CENTRE between beds of sickly plants. The three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails cross the BOTTOM of frame, a constable in a black tunic and helmet stands inside them at the LEFT, and a knot of men in caps stands at the rails with their backs to the camera. The dun fog lies over everything
shots.turn: an address -> a house with a look on it
shots.why: The house has to be a character before the body is, or the room that follows is only a room.

cuts.frame: Insert on one blank first-floor window of Number 3, a yellowed card standing in the corner of the pane with the two words "TO LET" in heavy black block capitals across it, the fog lying grey on the glass.
cuts.motion: The fog thickens across the pane by a hand's breadth and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on the words "TO LET".
cuts.camera: on the clay path inside the rails, angled up at the first floor, a 100mm lens turned on the one blank window. The fog lies grey between the lens and the glass
cuts.at_rest: One blank curtainless window of the first floor fills the frame, its black-painted sash weathered, its brickwork wet, a yellowed card standing in the corner of the lower pane, the two words "TO LET" standing in heavy black wood-type block capitals across its foxed buff face, the glass grey with fog, the room behind it dark and empty, the stone sill running across the BOTTOM of frame, the wet brick standing either side, and a streak of soot running down the render below the sill where the rain has carried it

shots.frame: Medium on Holmes on the pavement outside the rails, bare-headed above his overcoat collar, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the brick wall and its wooden rails crossing the BOTTOM of frame and the fogged house front rising behind him.
shots.motion: Holmes turns his head down from the house front to the ground at his boots and the camera pans a hand's breadth along the rails with him; his hands go behind his back; his chin lowers an inch.
shots.camera: on the pavement outside the wooden rails, level with Holmes's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned along the rails. The fogged house front rises behind him
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands on the pavement outside the rails, bare-headed above his overcoat collar, the bottle-green velvet showing at the open front, his head in the RIGHT half of frame. His hands are down at his sides and his eyes are on the house. The three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails cross the BOTTOM of frame, the constable and the knot of men in caps stand blurred behind him at the LEFT, and the brick front of Number 3 rises grey with fog beyond them
shots.turn: a hurry -> a man looking at the ground
shots.why: The chapter's own joke and its method in one picture: everyone expects him to rush in, and he reads the mud.

shots.frame: Insert straight down on the yellow clay path: boot prints crossing and overlapping each other in the wet, standing water in the deepest of them, the fringe of wet grass along the LEFT edge of frame.
shots.motion: Water settles in one deep print and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on the trampled clay.
shots.camera: above the clay path pointing straight down at the ground, a forearm and a half above the clay, a 50mm lens turned on the trampled surface. Flat fog-grey daylight falls on it from overhead
shots.at_rest: The narrow path of yellow clay and gravel fills the frame from edge to edge, boot prints crossing and overlapping each other across the whole of it, the clay pushed up in ridges between them, standing water lying in the deepest of the prints, the flat grey sky caught in that water, a fringe of wet grass along the LEFT edge of frame, one sickly plant standing in it, the gravel showing through where the clay has been scraped thin, and a low brick edging holding the bed back from the path at the RIGHT
shots.turn: trampled ground -> ground with a record in it
shots.why: The audience must see the mud as evidence before Watson fails to, or his failure means nothing.

cuts.frame: Insert closer on one square of the wet clay: a single square-toed boot print standing whole and sharp among the trampled ones, its edges clean where the others are smeared.
cuts.motion: A thin shadow crosses the clean print as a head comes between it and the sky, and the camera pushes straight in on the print.
cuts.camera: above the clay path pointing straight down, a forearm above the clay, a 100mm lens turned on one square of ground. Flat fog-grey daylight falls on it from overhead
cuts.at_rest: One square of the wet yellow clay fills the frame. A single square-toed boot print stands whole and sharp in the middle of it, its edges clean and its nailed sole pattern unbroken, the standing water in it still. Trampled and smeared half-prints of other boots lie all round it, their edges broken down into the wet. Small stones and pressed gravel show at the print's rim

shots.frame: Medium close on Watson halted on the clay path, bare-headed, sunburnt, thin waxed moustache, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the fogged house front rising behind him and the front door standing at the TOP of frame.
shots.motion: Watson's head turns from the ground up to the house front and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on his face; his mouth stays closed; his eyes narrow a little.
shots.camera: on the clay path inside the rails, level with Watson's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The fogged house front rises behind him and the front door stands at the TOP of frame
shots.at_rest: Watson stands halted on the narrow clay path, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, the brown tweed overcoat open over the tweed waistcoat and its watch chain. His head is a quarter of the frame's height and his hands are down at his sides. The brick front of Number 3 rises grey with fog behind him with the shut front door at the TOP of frame, and the sickly plants of the garden stand either side of the path
shots.turn: watching a method -> watching a man he cannot follow
shots.why: Watson's position for the whole episode, stated once in his face before the house swallows them.

shots.frame: Medium up the bare hall from the open front door: Gregson, a tall white-faced man in a dark coat standing at the far end with a notebook open in his hand, his back three-quarters to the camera, the stripped floorboards running up the CENTRE and the doorway to the front room open at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.motion: Gregson turns a quarter toward the open door and the camera pushes a hand's breadth up the hall; his notebook comes down to his side; his head tips toward the front room.
shots.camera: just inside the open front door at a standing man's eye height, square on up the hall, a 35mm lens turned along the stripped boards. The fog-grey daylight comes in past the lens from behind
shots.at_rest: The bare front hall runs away from the open front door, its stripped dusty floorboards going up the CENTRE of frame and the loose wallpaper hanging in strips from the plaster either side. Gregson, a tall white-faced man in a dark coat, stands at the far end with his back three-quarters to the camera and an open notebook in his hand. The doorway to the front room stands open at the TOP RIGHT, the stair rail shows at the LEFT edge, and the only light is the fog-grey daylight from the open door behind the camera
shots.turn: outside -> inside, and nothing touched
shots.why: The threshold beat, and the only place Gregson can be shown without spending a fourth voice on him.

cuts.frame: Insert on the loose wallpaper of the hall wall, a long strip hanging away from the plaster, the fog-grey daylight raking across the torn edge.
cuts.motion: The hanging strip lifts a thumb's width in the draught from the open door and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth.
cuts.camera: in the hall a foot from the wall, level with the torn edge of the paper, a 50mm lens turned on the plaster. The fog-grey daylight rakes across it from the LEFT
cuts.at_rest: A long strip of the hall's wallpaper hangs away from the plaster and falls across the frame, its torn edge curling, its printed face turned half away, the bare plaster behind it grey and blotched with damp, the paper's pattern faint on the wall where it has lifted, the fog-grey daylight from the open door raking across the torn edge from the LEFT, the hall beyond falling away dark, and the skirting board running along the BOTTOM of frame with its paint blistered off the wood

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes inside the hall with the open front door and its fog-grey daylight at the LEFT edge, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the loose-papered wall at the RIGHT, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes raises one hand and points back out through the open door as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his arm comes down across his coat; his eyes go to the front-room doorway.
shots.camera: in the hall with its back to the front room, level with Holmes's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The open front door and its daylight stand at the LEFT edge
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands inside the bare hall on the stripped boards, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet jacket open over the white shirt collar, his head a quarter of the frame's height. His lips are together with the line on them and one hand is down at his side. The open front door and its flat fog-grey daylight stand at the LEFT edge, the loose-papered wall with its hanging strips runs behind him at the RIGHT, and the dusty boards run away below the frame
shots.turn: everything untouched -> the path already ruined
shots.why: Holmes scoring off the official men is the chapter's running comedy, and it pays the garden path off.

shots.frame: Wide of the bare front room from the doorway: stripped dusty floorboards running away to the far wall, the tall curtainless window in the CENTRE of that wall giving flat fog-grey light, the white marble mantelpiece at the LEFT edge with a stump of red candle on it, and a well-dressed man lying on his back across the CENTRE of the floor.
shots.motion: The fog-grey light shifts a little across the boards and the camera pushes a hand's breadth in through the doorway toward the body.
shots.camera: in the front-room doorway at a standing man's eye height, square on across the room, a 35mm lens turned on the floor and the far wall. The doorway's edge stands at the RIGHT of frame
shots.at_rest: The bare front room stands empty but for one man. Stripped dusty floorboards run away from the doorway to the far wall, the tall curtainless window in the CENTRE of that wall giving flat fog-grey light into the room. The white marble mantelpiece stands at the LEFT edge with a stump of red candle burning low on it. A well-dressed man lies on his back across the CENTRE of the floor with his overcoat open, his arms out, and the dust lies undisturbed over most of the boards
shots.turn: an empty house -> a man dead in it
shots.why: The reveal the whole episode has been driving at, given the room's full width so the emptiness reads.

cuts.frame: Medium across the dusty floorboards: the dead man's shoulders and head on the boards, his overcoat open, the flat window light lying along the dust beside him.
cuts.motion: Dust turns in the window light above the boards and the camera pushes a hand's breadth in over the floor.
cuts.camera: on the boards a stride from the body, level with the dead man's shoulder and angled a little down, a 50mm lens turned along the floor. The window light comes flat from beyond him
cuts.at_rest: The dead man lies on his back on the stripped boards, his shoulders and head across the frame, his overcoat fallen open and his stiff white collar standing at his throat. The flat grey window light lies along the dust beside him and picks out the grain of the boards. His face is turned up and still, his hair dark against the pale floor, and the dust of the room lies undisturbed either side of him

shots.frame: Close on the dead man's face turned up from the boards, well fed and clean shaven above a stiff white collar, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the dust of the floor along the BOTTOM edge of frame.
shots.motion: The flat window light shifts a little across the still face and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on it.
shots.camera: on the boards beside the body, level with the dead man's face and a forearm from it, a 85mm lens turned down on him. The flat window light falls across the face from beyond
shots.at_rest: The dead man's face is turned up from the boards, well fed and clean shaven above the stiff white collar, the mouth a little open, the eyes closed, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his dark hair back against the pale dusty boards, the grey dust of the floor filling the BOTTOM edge of frame, the black of his overcoat collar at the LEFT, the flat fog-grey light from the tall window lying evenly on him, and the dark cloth of his shoulder running out of frame below his jaw
shots.turn: a body -> a man with a name
shots.why: A corpse is scenery until it has a name; the card is how the chapter gives it one.

cuts.frame: Insert on a printed visiting card held in a bare hand at the frame's CENTRE, the three lines "Enoch J. Drebber", "Cleveland" and "Ohio" standing in fine black copperplate script across it, the dusty floorboards below out of focus.
cuts.motion: The card turns a few degrees flat toward the camera and the camera pushes straight in on the engraved name "Enoch J. Drebber".
cuts.camera: on the boards beside the body, level with the held card and a forearm from it, a 50mm lens turned square on the printed face. The dusty boards fall away out of focus below
cuts.at_rest: A printed visiting card is held up in one bare hand at the CENTRE of frame, the thumb flat on its face and the fingers behind, three lines of fine black copperplate script standing across its face reading "Enoch J. Drebber", then "Cleveland", then "Ohio". The card is stiff yellowed ivory bristol board with square corners, faintly foxed with brown speckling. The stripped dusty floorboards lie below and behind, out of focus, and the flat fog-grey light from the tall window falls evenly on the card

shots.frame: Insert on the stripped floorboards beside the body: a dark smear of dried blood standing across two boards at the CENTRE of frame, the dust undisturbed either side of it, the dead man's shoulder at the TOP edge.
shots.motion: The window light creeps a finger's width along the boards and the camera pushes straight in on the dark smear.
shots.camera: on the boards beside the body, a forearm above the floor and angled straight down, a 50mm lens turned on the two boards. The window light creeps along them from beyond
shots.at_rest: A dark smear of dried blood stands across two stripped floorboards at the CENTRE of frame, its edges dried to brown and its body still dark where it pooled in the grain. The grey dust of the room lies undisturbed either side of it. The dead man's shoulder and the black of his overcoat stand at the TOP edge of frame, and the flat fog-grey light from the tall window lies along the boards
shots.turn: a death -> a death with no wound in it
shots.why: The puzzle stated as a picture: blood and no source for it, which is what makes the case a case.

shots.frame: Medium on Watson down on one knee on the dusty boards where Holmes has knelt, bare-headed, sunburnt, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the LEFT half, the tall window flat and grey in the CENTRE of the far wall behind him.
shots.motion: Watson lowers his head toward the boards and the camera pushes a hand's breadth in over the dust; his bare hand comes down flat beside the marks; his eyes travel along the floor.
shots.camera: on the boards across the room from Watson, level with his kneeling head and two yards from him, a 50mm lens turned on him and the floor. The tall window stands flat and grey behind him
shots.at_rest: Watson is down on one knee on the dusty boards where Holmes has knelt, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, the brown tweed overcoat open over the waistcoat and its watch chain, his right hand on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick set upright on the floor. His head is a quarter of the frame's height in the LEFT half. The tall curtainless window stands flat and grey in the CENTRE of the far wall behind him, the marble mantelpiece and its candle stump at the LEFT, and the dead man's boots show on the boards beyond
shots.turn: a spectator -> a man who tries to see
shots.why: THE TURN. Watson stops watching Holmes and tries to do what Holmes does. The episode's question is asked here and the room answers it.

cuts.frame: Insert straight down on the dusty boards where Watson is looking: grey dust, the overlapping half-prints of many boots, and one long scuff running away toward the far wall.
cuts.motion: The dust lifts a little where a breath crosses it and the camera pushes straight in on the trampled boards.
cuts.camera: above the boards where Watson is looking, pointing straight down, a forearm above the floor, a 50mm lens turned on the dust. Flat fog-grey light falls across it from the window
cuts.at_rest: The stripped floorboards fill the frame under a grey film of dust. The overlapping half-prints of many boots cross and recross the boards, their edges broken and their patterns trodden out of each other. One long scuff runs away toward the far wall, the dust pushed aside along it down to the bare grain. Every print lies broken across another under the grey film, and the flat window light lies evenly over all of it

shots.frame: Close on Watson's face low over the boards, bare-headed, sunburnt, thin waxed moustache, his head a third of the frame's height, the grey dust of the floor filling the BOTTOM of frame beneath him.
shots.motion: Watson's eyes come up off the floor toward the camera and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his jaw sets; his head lifts an inch.
shots.camera: on the boards level with Watson's face and a forearm and a half from it, low down at the floor, a 85mm lens turned up at him. The grey dust fills the frame beneath
shots.at_rest: Watson's face is low over the dusty boards, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, his head a third of the frame's height. The brown tweed of his shoulder stands at the LEFT edge and his stiff white collar shows at his throat. The grey dust of the floor fills the BOTTOM of frame beneath him, out of focus and close, and the flat fog-grey light from the tall window falls along his cheek
shots.turn: trying to see -> seeing mud
shots.why: The answer, on his own face: the method is not a thing you can simply decide to have.

shots.frame: Medium close on Lestrade in the dark corner, a small sallow sharp-featured man with dark eyes, bare-headed, his head a quarter of the frame's height, a lit match cupped in his hand at his chest, the peeled yellow plaster behind his shoulder.
shots.motion: Lestrade lifts the burning match up toward the bare plaster as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; the flame steadies; his eyes go to the wall.
shots.camera: in the corner of the front room, level with Lestrade's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The only light is the match cupped in his own hand
shots.at_rest: Lestrade stands in the darkest corner of the front room, a small lean sallow man with dark eyes set close, bare-headed, his wavy chestnut hair flat to the skull, the soft turned-down collar white at his throat above the charcoal frock coat. His head is a quarter of the frame's height and a lit match is cupped in his hand at his chest. The peeled yellow plaster of the corner stands behind his shoulder with the hanging paper curling away from it, and everything beyond the match light is dark
shots.turn: a rival -> a rival with something
shots.why: Lestrade earns the reveal, which is what makes Holmes's correction of it land at the end.

shots.frame: Insert on the yellow square of bare plaster filling the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, the word "RACHE" scrawled across it in blood-red letters, R then A then C then H then E, a smear trailing down from the last stroke, the hanging paper curling away at both edges.
shots.motion: The match light travels a hand's breadth across the plaster and the camera pushes straight in on the word "RACHE".
shots.camera: square on to the corner wall, level with the bared plaster and a long stride from it, a 50mm lens turned on the yellow square. The match light falls across it from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A square of bare yellow plaster fills the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge where the paper has been stripped away, the hanging paper curling off at both edges. The word "RACHE" stands scrawled across the plaster in blood-red letters, its five letters reading R, A, C, H, E, thick where the finger bore down, and a smear trails down from the last stroke where it has run. The plaster is coarse and pitted, and the corner beyond the match light is black
shots.turn: a bare wall -> a word on it
shots.why: The image the whole chapter is named for, given its own panel and no face to share it with.

cuts.frame: Insert closer on the last letter E of the word "RACHE", the blood-red stroke thick at its top and thinning down the coarse plaster where it has run.
cuts.motion: The match light swells across the letter and the camera pushes straight in on the running stroke.
cuts.camera: square on to the corner wall, a forearm from the plaster, a 100mm lens turned on the last letter. The match light swells across it from the LEFT
cuts.at_rest: The letter E fills the frame, the last letter of the word "RACHE", standing on the coarse yellow plaster of the stripped wall, its blood-red stroke thick at the top where the finger bore down, the stroke thinning as it runs down, one long drip hanging below it, the drip dry and glossy against the wall, the grain of the plaster standing up through the red, fine plaster grit caught in the dried blood at the letter's foot, bare pitted plaster filling the rest of the wall in frame, the torn wallpaper hanging away at the TOP of frame with its edge curling forward into the light, the match light lying along the stroke from the LEFT, the plaster beyond it standing in shadow, and the dark of the corner closing the edges of frame

shots.frame: Medium close on Lestrade turned from the wall with the match still burning low in his hand, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the LEFT half, the blood-red word "RACHE" standing on the plaster behind his shoulder at the RIGHT, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Lestrade turns his face from the wall to the camera as he speaks the line and the camera pulls back a hand's breadth; the match burns down toward his fingers; his chin comes up.
shots.camera: in the corner of the front room, level with Lestrade's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The match burns low in his own hand at the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Lestrade is turned from the wall with the match still burning low in his fingers, bare-headed, the wavy chestnut hair flat to his skull, the soft turned-down collar white above the charcoal frock coat. His head is a quarter of the frame's height in the LEFT half and his lips are together with the line on them. The blood-red word stands on the peeled yellow plaster behind his shoulder at the RIGHT, and the corner beyond the match light is dark
shots.turn: a word -> a woman's name
shots.why: Lestrade's reading has to be stated plainly and confidently, because the button is its refutation.

shots.frame: Medium on Holmes down on the dusty boards below the corner, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet showing at his open overcoat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the CENTRE, the peeled yellow plaster and its blood-red word "RACHE" on the wall above him.
shots.motion: Holmes lowers himself onto his forearms over the boards and the camera pushes a hand's breadth in over the dust; the magnifying glass comes down to the floor; his head turns along the skirting.
shots.camera: on the boards below the corner, level with Holmes's lowered shoulder and two yards from him, a 50mm lens turned on him and the floor. The peeled plaster and its word stand on the wall above
shots.at_rest: Holmes is down on the dusty boards below the corner, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet showing at his open overcoat, his head a quarter of the frame's height at the CENTRE. A large round magnifying glass is in one hand and a steel tape measure in the other. The peeled yellow plaster and its blood-red word stand on the wall above him, the hanging paper curling at the edges, and the grey dust of the floor runs away either side
shots.turn: a joke at his expense -> twenty minutes on his hands and knees
shots.why: The work itself, which the two detectives watch with contempt and which is the only thing in the room that will solve it.

cuts.frame: Insert on the dusty boards at the skirting: a steel tape measure run out flat along two boards and a large round magnifying glass laid beside it, a thin ink-stained hand at the frame's edge.
cuts.motion: The tape runs a hand's breadth further along the boards and the camera pushes straight in on the glass.
cuts.camera: above the boards at the skirting, pointing straight down, a forearm above the floor, a 50mm lens turned on the tape and the glass. The match light falls across them from the LEFT
cuts.at_rest: A steel tape measure is run out flat along two stripped boards at the skirting, its figures small and black along the edge, a large round magnifying glass lying beside it, the glass's brass rim bright, its lens clear over the grain, a thin ink-stained hand resting at the frame's edge, a small white sticking plaster round the middle joint of that forefinger, the grey dust lying over the boards either side, the skirting running across the TOP of frame with its paint blistered, and the nail heads standing proud of the grain

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes at the hall's far end with his overcoat buttoned, his head a quarter of the frame's height, the open front door and its fog-grey daylight at the LEFT edge and the loose-papered wall at the RIGHT, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes pulls his overcoat straight at the collar as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his hand comes down to his side; his eyes go past the camera to the door.
shots.camera: in the hall between the front room and the door, level with Holmes's eyes and a long stride from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The open front door stands at the LEFT edge and the papered wall at the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands at the hall's far end with his overcoat buttoned to the throat, bare-headed, his dark hair back from the high forehead, his head a quarter of the frame's height. His lips are together with the line on them and both hands are down at his sides. The open front door and its fog-grey daylight stand at the LEFT edge, the loose wallpaper hangs from the plaster at the RIGHT, and the stripped boards run away beneath him
shots.turn: an amateur -> a man who has already finished
shots.why: The deductions land as a list of things nobody else saw, which is the episode's question answered out loud.

shots.frame: Close on Watson in the hall, bare-headed, sunburnt, thin waxed moustache, his head a third of the frame's height, the loose-papered wall behind his shoulder and the fog-grey daylight from the open door along one cheek.
shots.motion: Watson's eyes travel from the front-room doorway round to the camera and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth on his face; his lips part a little; his chin lowers.
shots.camera: in the hall at the front-room doorway, level with Watson's eyes and a long stride from him, a 100mm lens turned on his face. The daylight from the open door lies along one cheek from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Watson stands in the bare hall on the stripped boards, bare-headed, sunburnt, the thin waxed moustache on his lip, the brown tweed overcoat open over the tweed waistcoat and its watch chain, his right hand closed on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick. His head is a third of the frame's height. The loose-papered wall stands behind his shoulder and the fog-grey daylight from the open front door lies along his near cheek from the LEFT
shots.turn: a room he stood in -> a room he never saw
shots.why: Watson's answer to his own question, on his face, before the button closes the door on it.

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes turned back in the open front doorway with the fog-grey street behind him, bare-headed above his buttoned overcoat collar, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the loose-papered hall wall at the LEFT edge, his lips together with the line on them.
shots.motion: Holmes turns his head back over his shoulder toward the hall as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; his hand comes to rest on the door edge; he turns away into the fog.
shots.camera: in the hall a stride inside the front door, level with Holmes's eyes, a 85mm lens turned on him in the doorway. The fog-grey street stands behind him and the papered wall at the LEFT edge
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands turned back in the open front doorway with his overcoat buttoned at the collar, bare-headed, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half. His lips are together with the line on them and one hand is at the door edge. The fog-grey street and the garden rails stand behind him through the open door, the loose-papered hall wall holds the LEFT edge, and the stripped boards run out under his boots
shots.turn: Rachel -> revenge
shots.why: THE BUTTON: the world's answer, spoken by the one man who has read it, on his way out of the door.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had read the man's whole history off the back of his hand.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A blue anchor tattooed on the hand, he said. A military carriage. There was the marine.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Then he threw me a note, and said he had been wrong about crime.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A bad business in the night, he said, and we might as well go and look.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: We drove out through a dun-coloured fog, and he talked to me about violins.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: No data yet. It is a mistake to theorise before you have the evidence.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A man lay dead across the city, and my friend discussed Cremona fiddles.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Number three wore an ill-omened look, and two of the four houses stood empty.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: I expected him to rush inside. He walked the pavement and stared at the mud.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The clay was printed over with a dozen boots, and rain had been at it all night.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Twice he stopped. Once he smiled. I could not see what there was to smile at.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A tall white-faced man met us and said nothing had been touched.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Except that, he said, pointing back at the trampled path behind us.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The room was bare, and the dead man lay in the middle of the floor.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Well dressed, and a card in his pocket: Enoch Drebber, of Cleveland, Ohio.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: There was blood in that room. There was no wound anywhere upon him.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: So I knelt where he had knelt, and tried to read the floor myself.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: I saw dust, and the marks of a dozen boots. Nothing else.

lines.speaker: g_lestrade
lines.text: I have made a discovery of the highest importance. Come here. Stand there.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: One word, scrawled across the bare plaster in letters of blood-red.

lines.speaker: g_lestrade
lines.text: Rachel. He was writing a woman's name, and was disturbed before he finished.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: For twenty minutes he crawled, measuring distances between things I could not see.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: Six feet high, in his prime, small feet, square-toed boots, a Trichinopoly cigar.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had watched a man I never saw.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: Rache is the German for revenge. Waste no time on Miss Rachel.
